title.en: Security tools: install carefully, investigate findings
title.ar: أدوات الأمن: الإعداد وفهم النتائج وإصلاحها
title.fr: Security tools: install carefully, investigate findings

objectives: Choose proxy, packet, port, dependency and source tools for distinct questions.
Constrain tool scope and interpret false positives and coverage limits.
Turn a dependency advisory into a reviewed update and regression.
introduction: Use each tool for a defined question against the local lab or your own source. Tool commands are computer instructions, not actions performed inside the Expo lesson viewer.

sections.title: Install from the publisher and record the environment
sections.text: Use the official installation page linked for each tool, select your operating system and architecture, and verify publisher signatures or published checksums where supplied. Do not paste a download-and-execute command from an unrelated tutorial. Record the installed version, operating system, target and configuration with results. Tools change their options and rule sets; consult the installed --help before assuming an old command still applies. Use a dedicated browser profile for proxy work so personal sessions do not enter captures. This course does not install these desktop tools on your device or claim they have all been executed. The provided Node lab and regression suite are a separate, reproducible baseline.

sections.title: OWASP ZAP: begin with manual exploration
sections.text: Install the desktop build from the ZAP project, start a temporary session and use Manual Explore with the exact local lab URL. Browse the known features through its configured browser and inspect the History and Alerts generated by passive analysis. Passive analysis reviews traffic you create; an automated spider or active scan sends additional requests and needs a deliberately chosen local scope. Keep the target limited to 127.0.0.1:4177, exclude unrelated origins and stop if a tool tries to leave it. Inspect the request and response behind each alert. A missing header alert can be valid but does not establish the same impact as another customer’s record being returned. Do not use Quick Start automated scanning against the named public projects as part of this lesson.

sections.title: Burp Suite Community: inspect and replay one request
sections.text: Install Community Edition from PortSwigger and open its dedicated browser for the lab. Add the exact loopback target to scope. Use Proxy history to find Alice’s successful order request, then send that request to Repeater. Change only order-a to order-b and compare unsafe and fixed modes. Turn interception off when it is merely pausing requests you want to observe. Community Edition supports useful manual workflows; do not promise a paid automated scanner feature as part of the free workflow. The lab uses HTTP, so you do not need to install a proxy certificate into the operating system for this exercise. If later studying HTTPS interception in an authorized lab, use an isolated profile and remove the temporary trust configuration afterward.

sections.title: Wireshark and Nmap answer different questions
sections.text: Wireshark observes packets on a chosen interface; it does not automatically decrypt every HTTPS session. Select the loopback capture interface for this lab, apply a capture/display filter appropriate to port 4177, make one health request, then stop capture. On Windows, loopback capture support may require the official capture driver provided by the installer. Avoid capturing an unrelated network interface with other people’s traffic. Nmap actively probes service endpoints. The bounded exercise is nmap -sT -p 4177 127.0.0.1, which asks whether the known local TCP port accepts a connection. An open port is an observation, not a vulnerability by itself. A filtered result does not prove a service absent; it reflects how the probe was answered or blocked.

sections.title: Dependency failures: why vulnerable packages matter
sections.text: Your application trusts direct dependencies and their transitive dependencies at build time and runtime. A known vulnerable package can expose a reachable parser or server feature; a compromised publisher or install script can affect the supply chain even before deployment. The necessary conditions depend on the advisory and how the application uses the package. A lockfile records a resolved dependency graph, but is not a guarantee that its contents are safe. Run npm audit --json from a disposable copy or controlled checkout and read the advisory, affected range, dependency path and proposed fix. An audit result can involve a development-only package or an unreachable feature, so explain applicability instead of blindly copying severity. Do not use npm audit fix --force as an unreviewed repair because it can introduce breaking changes.

sections.title: Dependabot and OSV-Scanner complement the review
sections.text: Enable Dependabot security/update features for a repository you control, with an explicit ecosystem and directory schedule. Review its pull request like any other code change: lockfile differences, release notes, tests and runtime behavior. A merged update is not verified remediation until the affected build is deployed and the relevant behavior retested. OSV-Scanner compares supported source/lockfile information with vulnerability records; a current source-scan example is osv-scanner scan source -r . from the intended repository. Record the scanner version and data freshness. These tools can report a known advisory; they cannot prove that unknown vulnerabilities do not exist or that every exploit precondition is present in your deployment.

sections.title: Semgrep and header checks need interpretation
sections.text: Semgrep applies source-analysis rules. Install it using the official supported method, choose a reviewed local configuration or an explicitly selected rule set, and scan the intended source directory. Check the source-to-sink path rather than treating every pattern match as a proven exploit. A parameterized database call may look superficially similar to an unsafe call; wrappers can also hide a real issue from a simple rule. For a SecurityHeaders-style exercise, inspect the local /health and homepage response headers with DevTools or Invoke-WebRequest. Explain what each policy does and whether the response context requires it. Do not send private staging URLs to third-party analysis services without checking authorization and data-sharing implications.

sections.title: A professional finding workflow
sections.text: For every alert, record the tool/version, exact scope, rule or advisory id, evidence, affected code path, confidence, impact and a remediation owner. Mark false positives with an explanation and a review date rather than deleting every inconvenient result. Fix the smallest relevant cause, add a regression or repeatable verification, and rerun the applicable check. A dependency upgrade should preserve the application’s test suite and remove the affected resolved version or document why the advisory no longer applies. Darija: الأداة كتعطي إشارة؛ خاصك تفهم الطريق من المدخل حتى التأثير قبل ما تسميها ثغرة مؤكدة. Clean output is bounded evidence about the rules and versions you ran, never a blanket security guarantee.

examples.code:
nmap -sT -p 4177 127.0.0.1
npm audit --json
osv-scanner scan source -r .

annotations.label: Probe only the known loopback lab port after installing Nmap from its publisher.
Review dependency advisories from the intended repository; this may contact the configured package registry.
Inspect supported source and lockfiles with the installed OSV-Scanner version; review results rather than applying blind updates.

exercises.task: Choose a tool for packet inspection, replaying one HTTP request, reviewing a known package advisory and finding suspicious source patterns.
hints: Each tool has a different evidence boundary.
exercises.solution:
Packets: Wireshark
HTTP replay: Burp Repeater or ZAP request tooling
Dependency advisory: npm audit / OSV-Scanner / Dependabot
Source patterns: Semgrep
exercises.walkthrough: No tool replaces the others, and none establishes all application security properties.

exercises.task: Write a remediation record for a fictional vulnerable transitive parser. Do not invent a real CVE.
hints: Mark the advisory as fictional and include a dependency path.
exercises.solution:
Fictional advisory -> app > importer > parser
Check affected versions and used parsing feature
Upgrade compatible parent/package in a branch
Review lockfile and release notes
Run parser regression and app tests
Deploy and verify resolved version
exercises.walkthrough: The workflow handles both applicability and the risk of breaking the application during repair.

quiz.question: Does a ZAP passive alert prove exploitability?
options: No; inspect its evidence and context.
Yes; every alert is a confirmed breach.
answerExplanations: Correct. Tool observations require applicability review.
Not quite. Tool observations require applicability review.

quiz.question: Which Burp Community workflow is used here?
options: A promised paid automated scanner feature.
Manual request inspection and Repeater comparison.
quiz.explanation: The exercise uses capabilities appropriate to Community Edition.
answerExplanations: Not quite. The exercise uses capabilities appropriate to Community Edition.
Correct. The exercise uses capabilities appropriate to Community Edition.

quiz.question: What should Wireshark capture for this exercise?
options: Only the local lab interface/traffic.
Every nearby user’s traffic.
quiz.explanation: Capture scope should match authorization and necessity.
answerExplanations: Correct. Capture scope should match authorization and necessity.
Not quite. Capture scope should match authorization and necessity.

quiz.question: Does an open Nmap port prove a vulnerability?
options: Yes; all listening services are insecure.
No; it proves an observed service endpoint.
quiz.explanation: A service must be evaluated in context.
answerExplanations: Not quite. A service must be evaluated in context.
Correct. A service must be evaluated in context.

quiz.question: Is a lockfile proof all packages are safe?
options: No; it records resolved dependencies.
Yes; locked packages cannot contain flaws.
quiz.explanation: Reproducibility and security are distinct properties.
answerExplanations: Correct. Reproducibility and security are distinct properties.
Not quite. Reproducibility and security are distinct properties.

quiz.question: Should npm audit fix --force be applied without review?
options: Yes; security updates cannot break behavior.
No; inspect compatibility and tests.
quiz.explanation: Forced updates can change dependency contracts.
answerExplanations: Not quite. Forced updates can change dependency contracts.
Correct. Forced updates can change dependency contracts.

quiz.question: What does a dependency path help establish?
options: How the affected package enters the application.
Which customer owns an order.
quiz.explanation: Reachability and update strategy depend on the graph.
answerExplanations: Correct. Reachability and update strategy depend on the graph.
Not quite. Reachability and update strategy depend on the graph.

quiz.question: Can Semgrep have false negatives?
options: No; source scanning proves every path safe.
Yes; rules and analysis have limits.
answerExplanations: Not quite. Static analysis coverage is bounded.
Correct. Static analysis coverage is bounded.

quiz.question: Should a private staging URL be submitted to an external checker automatically?
options: No; review authorization and data exposure first.
Yes; every checker is part of your trusted environment.
quiz.explanation: Third-party services create another data-sharing boundary.
answerExplanations: Correct. Third-party services create another data-sharing boundary.
Not quite. Third-party services create another data-sharing boundary.

quiz.question: When is a package repair verified?
options: As soon as a bot opens a pull request.
After the reviewed change, relevant tests and deployed-version check.
quiz.explanation: A proposed change is not an implemented, running repair.
answerExplanations: Not quite. A proposed change is not an implemented, running repair.
Correct. A proposed change is not an implemented, running repair.

steps.detail: Locate the request, dependency path or source match.

steps.title: Applicability
steps.detail: Determine whether the preconditions exist and reproduce locally.

steps.title: Repair and retest
steps.detail: Review the change and verify both security and ordinary functionality.

glossary: A reported candidate that does not establish the claimed weakness in context.
A package required by another dependency.
A record of resolved dependency versions and related metadata.
